sources.title: Apache Flink Agents 0.3.1 Release Announcement
sources.summary: Bug-fix release of the Flink Agents 0.3 series, released 2026-07-25 by Wenjin Xie.

facts.claim: Flink Agents 0.3.1 released July 25, 2026, described as the first bug fix release of the Flink Agents 0.3 series
0.3.1 includes 5 bug fixes, Flink 2.3 distribution support (now default), and installer improvements
Fixes address Python gateway initialization, state deserialization during recovery, prompt placeholder substitution, Java tool schema parsing, and Anthropic chat model crashes
Supported chat model providers as of 0.3.1: OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama, Azure AI, AWS Bedrock, Google Gemini
Supported vector stores as of 0.3.1: Elasticsearch, Milvus, OpenSearch, S3Vectors

sources.relevance_to_us: Flink Agents supports Ollama as a chat-model provider natively as of 0.3.x -- direct path for a Flink job on NvidiaSpark-1 to call a local Ollama/vLLM endpoint if vLLM is exposed as an OpenAI-compatible provider. Flink 2.3 default distro matters for CSA 1.5 which is still on Flink 1.20 -- version skew to plan for in ch11.
feeds: ch11 Flink on GPU + Flink Agents

sources.title: Apache Flink Agents 0.3.0 Release Announcement
sources.summary: Major 0.3.0 release, 2026-06-19, adds Agent Skills, Mem0 long-term memory, YAML declarative API, cross-language Python/Java actions; still explicitly a preview with breaking-change risk.

facts.claim: 0.3.0 released June 19, 2026
Adds Agent Skills for packaging prompts and tools; Mem0-based long-term memory replacing the previous vector-store implementation; a durable reconciler for side effects during failure recovery
Adds a YAML declarative API for agent configuration with JSON Schema validation, and cross-language actions enabling Python-Java interoperability
New chat models: Amazon Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, OpenAI Responses API. New embedding models: Amazon Bedrock, Tongyi. New vector stores: Amazon OpenSearch, Amazon S3 Vectors, Milvus, Mem0
Apache Fluss (Incubating) now supported as an action state store backend alongside Kafka
"The current APIs and configuration options are experimental and may undergo non-backward compatible changes in future versions" -- stability expected only after 1.0

sources.relevance_to_us: Confirms Flink Agents is pre-1.0 and API-unstable -- ch11 should flag this as an evaluation/demo technology, not production-pin. Kafka-backed state store option is directly compatible with the existing CSM/Strimzi Kafka on WindowsDesktop and would be on NvidiaSpark-1 too.
feeds: ch11 Flink on GPU + Flink Agents

sources.title: Flink 1.20 docs: External Resource Framework
sources.summary: Official Flink 1.20 doc page for the external-resource / GPU plugin framework, including Kubernetes NVIDIA device plugin integration.

facts.claim: "For Kubernetes deployment, administrators should make sure the NVIDIA GPU device plugin is installed. Notice the required version is 1.10+."

Config keys: `external-resources: gpu`, `external-resource.gpu.amount: 2`, `external-resource.gpu.driver-factory.class: org.apache.flink.externalresource.gpu.GPUDriverFactory`, `external-resource.gpu.kubernetes.config-key: nvidia.com/gpu`
Optional GPU plugin params: `discovery-script.path` and `discovery-script.args` (defaults to the bundled NVIDIA discovery script)
Operators read GPU info via `RuntimeContext`/`FunctionContext.getExternalResourceInfos(String resourceName)`, returning entries with an "index" key for each GPU device index

sources.relevance_to_us: This is the concrete mechanism for ch11: Flink 1.20 (the version CSA 1.5 ships) has a built-in GPU external-resource plugin that talks to the standard k8s NVIDIA device plugin -- directly usable on a k3d cluster on NvidiaSpark-1 with the NVIDIA device plugin installed, same config keys apply.

facts.claim: "Apache Flink Kubernetes Operator (Flink Operator) 1.11.0 and Apache Flink (Flink) 1.20" is the foundation for CSA Operator 1.4.0

sources.title: Cloudera Streaming Analytics Operator 1.5.0 -- What's New
sources.summary: CSA Operator 1.5.0: Materialized View Engine on k8s, async Flink job handling, Flink Kubernetes Operator upgraded to 1.13, Postgres 18.1, OpenJDK 17. Still built on Flink 1.20 (Aug 2024). No Flink Agents/GPU/aarch64 content.

facts.claim: "Materialized Views to maintain mutating snapshots of queried data, which can be accessed through REST APIs" added for SQL Stream Builder on Kubernetes
Flink job handling is now asynchronous, improving Streaming SQL Console responsiveness and stabilizing job status transitions
Embedded Flink Kubernetes Operator upgraded to version 1.13
PostgreSQL default bumped to 18.1; Docker images now use OpenJDK 17 with support for older cipher suites
This release still builds on Apache Flink 1.20 (released August 2024) with Flink Kubernetes Operator 1.13 (announced September 2025); no Flink Agents, GPU, aarch64, or AI features mentioned

sources.title: nifi-python-extensions: ParseDocument.py
sources.summary: Source-derived property list for ParseDocument, a document-parsing/OCR processor feeding NiFi's chunking pipeline (ParseDocument -> ChunkDocument -> Put[Qdrant|Chroma]).

facts.claim: ParseDocument "Parses incoming unstructured text documents and performs optical character recognition (OCR) in order to extract text from PDF and image files," output as JSON-lines with 'text' and 'metadata' keys

Properties: Input Format (Plain Text/HTML/Markdown/PDF/Word/Excel/PowerPoint), PDF Parsing Strategy (Automatic/High Resolution/OCR Only/Fast), PDF Parsing Model (yolox/detectron2_onnx/chipper), Element Strategy, Include Page Breaks, Infer Table Structure, Languages (default "Eng"), Metadata Fields (default "filename, uuid"), Include Extracted Metadata
No embedding-model or LLM-endpoint config exists on this processor -- it is pure document extraction using LangChain loaders, upstream of embedding/vector-store processors

sources.relevance_to_us: Confirms the intended NiFi 2 RAG chain shape: ParseDocument -> ChunkDocument -> PutQdrant/PutChroma, with QueryQdrant on the retrieval side. Useful skeleton for ch10 pipeline diagrams.

sources.title: vLLM on the DGX Spark: Architecture, Configuration, and Local Evaluation
sources.summary: Official vLLM blog (2026-06-01) benchmarking vLLM's OpenAI-compatible server on a real DGX Spark GB10, serving Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-NVFP4.

facts.claim: Decode throughput measured at 22.7-23.7 tokens/second across five scenarios serving Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-NVFP4 (120B params, ~12B active, NVFP4 quantized) on DGX Spark
Prefill throughput: ~140 tok/s for short prompts, 1,877-1,884 tok/s for long prompts
Config used: `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.85`, `--max-model-len 131072`, `--max-num-seqs 4`, Docker image `vllm/vllm-openai:cu130-nightly`
"Initial weight load is a separate problem from request warmup. If the 10-15 minute safetensor load time matters for your deployment, evaluate vLLM's fastsafetensors or InstantTensor loading paths."
Provides "an OpenAI-compatible API with the memory, batching, KV-cache, and telemetry controls needed to run large NVFP4 models locally," `/v1` endpoints at `http://localhost:8000/v1`

sources.relevance_to_us: This is the OpenAI-compatible endpoint ch10/ch11 would point NiFi's PromptChatGPT/QueryOpenAI processor or a Flink Agents OpenAI chat-model config at on NvidiaSpark-1 -- concrete port (:8000/v1) and image tag to reuse. Overlaps ch4/ch6 but directly load-bearing here since it's the exact plug point for NiFi->LLM and Flink Agents->LLM.

load_bearing_claims.claim: Flink Agents 0.3.1 (2026-07-25) natively supports Ollama as a chat-model provider, alongside OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure AI, AWS Bedrock, and Google Gemini.
load_bearing_claims.why_it_matters: This is the single fact that makes ch11's 'Flink Agents on NvidiaSpark-1 calling a local model' story concrete rather than speculative -- Ollama support is built-in, not something to hand-roll via a generic OpenAI-compatible shim.

load_bearing_claims.claim: Flink Agents remains pre-1.0 with an explicit warning that APIs and config 'may undergo non-backward compatible changes in future versions' until 1.0.
load_bearing_claims.why_it_matters: Sets expectations for the guide: ch11 should present Flink Agents as an evaluation/demo capability on NvidiaSpark-1, not a production commitment, and should pin an exact version (0.3.1) rather than 'latest'.

load_bearing_claims.claim: CSA Operator 1.5.0 (Steven's current production version target) is still built on Apache Flink 1.20 and Flink Kubernetes Operator 1.13, with zero mention of Flink Agents, GPU, or aarch64 in its release notes.
load_bearing_claims.why_it_matters: Confirms Flink Agents + GPU support are NOT things CSO ships out of the box -- any ch11 demo is bolt-on integration work layered on top of the stock CSA operator, which the guide must say explicitly rather than imply as a Cloudera-supported feature.

load_bearing_claims.claim: Flink 1.20's external resource framework has a built-in GPU plugin (external-resource.gpu.*) that integrates with the standard Kubernetes NVIDIA device plugin (v1.10+ required).
load_bearing_claims.why_it_matters: This is the mechanism ch11 needs for 'Flink on GPU' on k3d/NvidiaSpark-1 -- it is stock upstream Flink 1.20 functionality (the exact version CSA 1.5 embeds), so no version upgrade is required to get GPU-aware TaskManagers, only device-plugin installation on the k3d cluster.

load_bearing_claims.claim: vLLM's own DGX Spark benchmark exposes an OpenAI-compatible /v1 API at http://localhost:8000/v1 serving Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-NVFP4 at 22.7-23.7 tok/s decode.
load_bearing_claims.why_it_matters: Gives ch10/ch11 a concrete, vendor-verified endpoint shape and realistic throughput number for 'NiFi/Flink Agents calling a Spark-hosted LLM' rather than an assumed number; also matches the same :8000 port convention Steven already uses for vLLM on WindowsDesktop, easing the demo narrative.
